The exchange rate is the trading base rate announced by the Export-Import Bank of Korea (won/dollar 1,342.70 won, won/yen 842.95 won, won/yuan 201.43 won), and the oil price is the closing price of the shortened Thanksgiving day (11/26) (WTI January contract $85.64, Brent $92.32) and Dubai oil announced by Offinet on 11/26. It's $87.00. Gold and silver spot prices as of the morning of 11/27. The LME official price is the latest value as of November 25th (spot settlement price for zinc, lead, nickel, and tin, 3-month futures price for copper and aluminum), and the Public Procurement Service release price is the sale price as of November 27th. China's petrochemical spot (SunSirs) and BDI prices are as of November 26th, and China's three major futures exchanges have intraday values ​​as of the morning of November 27th. Due to the Thanksgiving holiday, CBOT grain prices are the latest from the night session of November 25th (early morning on November 26th, Korean time), and CFR Japan (MOPJ) naphtha valuation prices are from November 25th. The latest Bank of Korea price index is from October, and the latest index Nuri petrochemical prices is from the third quarter of 2026.

daily.label: Daily
daily.summary: As of 11:10 a.m. on Friday, November 27th. The standard won/dollar trading rate was lowered to 1,342.70 won (−1.20 won), and the won/yen is 842.95 won, and the won/yuan is 201.43 won. Oil prices are maintaining the values ​​they jumped during the shortened Thanksgiving market — WTI January contract closed at $85.64 (+2.3%) on 11/26 from $83.68 on 11/25, and Brent $92.32 and Dubai crude contract closed at $87.00 (+3.3%). Precious metals were strong with gold at $3,616.46 (+0.5%) and silver at $43.01 (+2.4%), and in Chinese futures, copper soared to 92,220 yuan (+3.9%) and Shanghai crude oil +1.1%, DCE EG +3.1%, and LLDPE +1.8% rose together. The Public Procurement Service's emission prices rose all at once to KRW 4,800,000 (+3.5%) for aluminum, KRW 17,900,000 (+2.0%) for copper, and KRW 2,990,000 (+2.8%) for lead. Chinese spot prices rose to +2.5% for PVC and +1.3% for LDPE and fell for -2.4% for PP and -1.7% for PC, and BDI was 3,152 points (+1.5%), the highest since September 29.

weekly.label: Weekly
weekly.summary: This is the closing flow for the fourth week of November (11/23~11/27). Compared to the closing price of the previous Friday (11/20), WTI rose 2.7% from 83.41 to $85.64, Brent rose from 92.57 to $92.32 (-0.3%), and Dubai Oil remained flat from 87.41 to $87.00 (-0.5%). The won is 0.9% weaker than the dollar (1,330.80 → 1,342.70 won). Precious metals were strong at +2.2% for gold and +4.2% for silver, while the LME continued to be weak at -10.5% for aluminum, -4.3% for copper, and -4.1% for zinc (based on 11/25 official prices). Chinese petrochemical spot prices fell to PP -6.8%, PC -2.6%, and benzene -2.0%, and BDI rose 8.8% from 2,898 to 3,152 points, showing the largest increase this week.

highlights.title: WTI $85.64 — surges 2.3% on shortened Thanksgiving day
highlights.text: WTI January contract rose 2.3% from $83.68 settled on 11/25 to $85.64 shortened on 11/26. Brent also rose 1.9% from 90.64 to $92.36, and Offinet Dubai Oil price jumped 3.3% from $84.19 on 11/25 to $87.00 on 11/26. The 11/27 Asian session was flat at $85.64.

highlights.title: Won/Dollar 1,342.70 Won — Weekly weakness of 0.9%
highlights.text: The standard won/dollar trading rate was 1,342.70 won on 11/27, down 1.20 won from the previous day. Compared to 1,330.80 won on the previous Friday (11/20), it is 11.90 won (0.9%) weaker. The won/yen is 842.95 won, and the won/yuan is 201.43 won.

highlights.title: Chinese copper futures 92,220 yuan (+3.9%) — led by late-week rebound
highlights.text: SHFE copper was at 92,220 yuan on the morning of 11/27, up 3.9% from the previous day's settlement of 88,770 yuan. Shanghai crude oil rose 600.70 yuan (+1.1%), DCE EG 5,289 yuan (+3.1%), and LLDPE 8,314 yuan (+1.8%), and the Public Procurement Service's emission price also increased to 17,900,000 won (+2.0%) for copper and 4,800,000 won (+3.5%) for aluminum.

highlights.title: BDI 3,152 — highest since September 29
highlights.text: The Baltic dry cargo rate index rose to 3,152 points (+45, +1.45%) on 11/26, the highest since September 29. All ships increased to 5,100 (+86) for Capesize, 2,273 (+50) for Panamax, and 1,816 (+2) for Supramax.

monthly.label: Monthly
monthly.badge: Confirmed in October, tentative in November
monthly.summary: The October confirmed notice and the published values from November 1 to 20 are placed side by side. Oil and copper prices fell significantly in November from their peak in October, and the food index and domestic grain import prices moved slowly.

highlights.title: High in October → Plunge in November
highlights.text: The monthly average for WTI spot is $102.07 in October → $92.71 (−9.2%) from November 1 to 17, and for Brent, it is 123.93 → $95.98 (−22.6%). The futures closing price on November 20 was WTI $83.98, which is lower than the monthly average.

highlights.title: Monthly average for copper -6.4%, aluminum and nickel rise
highlights.text: The LME spot monthly averages fell to 14,532 → $13,608 for copper, 3,820 → $3,792 for zinc, and rose to 3,061 → $3,145 for aluminum and 15,470 → $15,752 for nickel. Copper October averages were the highest of the year.

highlights.title: Food prices fall for the first time in 5 months
highlights.text: The FAO food price index in October was 133.9 (−1.2%), with grains at 116.8 (−4.5%), led by wheat and corn. The domestic import price is $299.69 (-0.13%) for wheat, $273.46 (+1.23%) for corn, and $555.61 (+1.82%) for soybeans.

highlights.title: Exchange rate is flat, NAFTA is -10%
highlights.text: The monthly average of won and dollar is almost unchanged from 1,337.66 won in October to 1,338.91 won from 1 to 20 November. Naphtha (CFR Japan) is -10.4% from 991.98 → $888.69. Petrochemical PC was +1.70% in October and returned to -0.94% in the third week of November.

yearly.label: Yearly
yearly.badge: Compared to the beginning of the year
yearly.summary: Fluctuations through November 20 compared to the end of 2025 (or December 2025 average). Oil prices and shipping rose significantly, and gold hit an all-time high before falling lower than at the beginning of the year.

highlights.title: Oil price +46%, March is a watershed month
highlights.text: WTI is +46.3% from $57.42 at end-2025 to $83.98 on 11/20. Due to the Middle East crisis in March, it soared to $119.48 on March 9 and then went through an adjustment, and is +25.3% compared to the end of February ($67.02).

highlights.title: Gold falls after an all-time high
highlights.text: It hit an all-time high of $5,318.40 (COMEX closing price) on January 29th and fell to $3,515.40 on 11/20, -19.0% compared to the beginning of the year. During the same period, silver fell further by -42.69%.

highlights.title: Copper's increase from +23% increased to +3.6%
highlights.text: Copper rose to a monthly average of $14,532 in October, +23.1% compared to the beginning of the year, but fell sharply in November, reaching a spot price of $12,230.50 (+3.6%) on 11/20. Aluminum +10.7%, zinc +16.1%, nickel +2.9%.

highlights.title: Shipping +54%, exchange rate -7%
highlights.text: BDI is +54.4% from 1,877 to 2,898 at the end of 2025. The won/dollar price was -7.1% from 1,439.0 won to 1,336.2 won, or the monthly average of 1,527.30 won in June was the highest point of the year.

recycled.label: Recycled materials
recycled.range: Survey conducted in November 2026 (posted and announced on 2026-11-25)
recycled.summary: This is the November 2026 version of the Nationally Approved Statistics (No. 392001) “Recyclable Resource Price Survey,” which is surveyed by the Korea Environment Corporation on the 10th of every month and published on the 26th. It is the national average, won/kg, including value-added tax and excluding logistics costs. It is the sales price after intermediate processing for waste plastic, waste glass bottles, and waste metal cans, and the purchase price of unprocessed raw materials from intermediate processing companies for waste paper and steel scrap. Among the 26 items, ABS flake was removed from the table as it was not announced (-) this month. While waste metals fell significantly again (aluminum cans -5.9%, steel scrap -5.1%), waste paper and PVC flakes rose.

highlights.title: Aluminum cans plummeted -5.9% for two consecutive months
highlights.text: Aluminum cans fell 148.6 won (−5.9%) from 2,502.1 won in October to 2,353.5 won in November. This is a 17.8% decrease in two months from 2,863.4 won in September. Steel scrap was flat from 346.1 won to 328.6 won (−5.1%), and steel cans were flat at 342.7 won. During the same period, LME aluminum spot prices fell 8.7% from $3,120.5 per ton to $2,849.0 per ton.

highlights.title: Recycled pellets remained flat — only PS rose
highlights.text: There was no significant change at KRW 983.9 (−0.2%) for PE pellets, KRW 783.9 (−0.4%) for PP pellets, and KRW 1,437.0 (flat) for ABS pellets, and only PS pellets rose from KRW 1,245.0 to KRW 1,255.7 (+0.9%). EPS ingots are at KRW 534.7 (−1.7%), and EPS pellets are at KRW 926.9 (+0.1%).

highlights.title: Colorless and composite PET declined, colored remained unchanged.
highlights.text: PET colorless flakes fell from KRW 1,133.3 to KRW 1,120.6 (−1.1%), and composite flakes fell from KRW 426.5 to KRW 410.5 (−3.8%). Colored flakes were flat at 488.6 won, and PET compression rose to 607.7 won (+0.8%).

highlights.title: Abolition rises for three consecutive months, PVC flakes rebound
highlights.text: There has been an upward trend since August, with waste corrugated cardboard rising from 93.5 won to 93.9 won (+0.4 won), and waste newspaper rising from 125.8 won to 126.6 won (+0.8 won). PVC flake rebounded from 534.1 won to 540.8 won (+1.3%), while PP compression was mixed at 379.2 won (+0.3%) and PE compression was 467.6 won (-0.9%).

It is the average of the prices of survey companies in 8 regions nationwide (excluding Jeju), and the metropolitan area value in each row is the average of Seoul, Incheon, and Gyeonggi. The published price may differ from the actual transaction price depending on the region, quality, processing stage, and transaction conditions, so you must check the research standards for contracts and bids. The next announcement (for December 2026) is scheduled for the next weekday, 2026-12-28, as 2026-12-26 is a Saturday. The survey items for this statistics are 2 waste paper, 17 waste plastics (PE·PP·PS·ABS·PVC·PET·EPS), 3 waste glass bottles, 3 waste metals (steel scrap, iron cans, aluminum cans), and 1 waste tire. Engineering resins such as PC, PMMA, and PBT and waste copper (copper) scrap were not investigated and were not loaded.

notes: All prices are confirmed from free and public sources. Paid index-only items are not estimated and not indicated.

The LME zinc, lead, nickel, and tin are the LME official spot (Cash) settlement price (11/25: zinc 3,520.50, lead 1,792.00, nickel 15,035.00, tin $38,200.00), and the copper and aluminum in the table are the 3-month futures official price (11/25: copper) 11,758.00·Aluminum $2,760.00), so the standards are different. The 11/26 official price had not yet been published at the time of inquiry, so the 11/25 value was retained. The source is the Westmetall table, which is a direct translation of the LME official price.
Petrochemical and plastic raw materials are priced at domestic Chinese spot prices (yuan/ton), which differ from Korean import negotiators depending on grade, volume, and freight.

Nafta was carried in two ways. The CFR Japan (MOPJ) public valuation is $801.25/ton (11/25, +1.6%), and the Singapore spot price of Offinet (Korea National Oil Corporation) international petroleum product price is $88.09/barrel (11/26, $85.86 the previous day). The units are different so they cannot be directly compared.

BDI, Capesize, Panamax, and Supramax are the Baltic Shipping Exchange indices and are the closing prices on Thursday, November 26 (BDI 3,152, BCI 5,100, BPI 2,273, BSI 1,816). BDI is at its highest since September 29th.

The FAO food and grain price index is a monthly index and is the October 2026 value (announced on November 6). The FAO announcement is 133.9 (−1.6 points, −1.2%) for food and 116.8 (−5.5 points, −4.5%) for grains, which is slightly different from the KREI screen display (−1.7 points for food).

CBOT wheat and corn are carried forward to March, carrying the closing prices of previous months in cents/bushel, and soybeans are carried to January. Since November 26th is closed for Thanksgiving, the 11/25 night session (11/26 dawn Korean time) values ​​are the latest, and the night session on November 27th resumed at 10 a.m. Korean time. The domestic import price is USD/ton based on customs clearance in October 2026 according to the Agricultural and Fishery Products Trade Information.

Crypto is traded 24 hours a day and has different reference days. The price and fluctuation rate are based on the CoinGecko dollar spot and 24-hour fluctuation rate, and the won price is based on the Upbit won market at the same time.
LME copper and aluminum are based on 3-month futures prices, and spot settlement prices are written in the notes for each item.

The Public Procurement Service's stockpile release price includes VAT and is a sales price within the limits of registered actual consumers, and cannot be directly compared with the LME international price. In the 11/27 announcement, there were only aluminum, copper, and lead, so tin maintained its value of 11/26.

Korea Petrochemical Association (KPIA) raw material and resin prices were not included because they cannot be checked for free. kpia.or.kr had a connection error (500·503) and the association's data was moved to kcia.kr (Korea Chemical Industry Association), and the association's price and statistics DB is only for paid users (1.2 million won per year, 2 devices). No estimates were included.

The exchange rate is the trading standard rate announced by the Export-Import Bank of Korea (announced once a business day, around 11 a.m.), and is different from the exchange rate at bank counters and card payments. The 11/27 notice was 1,342.70 won/dollar, 842.95 won/yen, 201.43 won/yuan, all slightly lower than 11/26 (1,343.90, 844.37, 201.57).

Chinese futures are the values ​​of the main contracts of the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE), Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE), and Zhengzhou Commodity Exchange (ZCE) read at the Sina Finance delayed price. This is the intraday value on the morning of November 27th, and the previous day's value is the settlement price on November 26th.
SHFE copper/aluminum is yuan/ton, Shanghai Crude Oil (SC) is yuan/barrel. The LME dollar notation and the exchange rate, VAT, and rating are different, so direct comparison is not possible.
The fluctuations of DCE PP·LLDPE·PVC·EG and ZCE PTA·methanol were calculated as the difference from the settlement price on November 26.

SCFI·CCFI is a container freight index released every Friday by the Shanghai Shipping Exchange (SSE). Only the comprehensive index is released, and detailed indices for each route are provided to paid subscribers.

The SMM production copper premium carried the figure specified in the SMM public article (11/23 warrant average of $450/ton, −$45 compared to the previous day). The 11/24 public value could not be confirmed, so the 11/23 value was kept, and the dashboard value is only visible after logging in.

The KOMIS (Korea Resources Information Service) screen could not confirm the values ​​even in this update, so 6 types of non-ferrous metals were filled in with the Westmetall table, which was copied directly from the LME official notice. Spot settlement price and 3-month futures price are shown separately.

Index Nuri petrochemical raw material prices are based on CFR Northeast Asia since 2012 based on a survey by the Korea Chemical Industry Association (KCIA), and the latest value in the public table is the average for the third quarter of 2026 (updated on October 30). This is not the actual price of domestic won.

KAMIS wholesale price is the wholesale market middleman sales price (national average), confirmed as of November 25th (59,640 won for 20 kg of rice product, the same since 11/13). For soybeans (40kg of domestically produced white beans), the November 20th survey was the latest confirmed value, so I left it as is. Surveys conducted after 11/26 were not confirmed in this inquiry.

The Bank of Korea's producer price index and import price index are provisional values for October 2026 (2020=100). The producer price index was announced on November 20th, and the import price index was announced on November 13th.

Import unit prices for the most recent month by item and HS code from the Korea Customs Service's export and import trade statistics (tradedata.go.kr) were not confirmed on the first public screen, so they were not included in this update.

The operation rate and inventory indicators of SCI99 (intl.sci99.com) were not included because they are for paid members only. The PP·LLDPE values ​​from the public price center on the same site are not included in the table because the items overlap with the existing Chinese spot products (SunSirs).

The Korea Nonferrous Metals Association (nonferrous.or.kr) discloses the spot prices of the six LME nonferrous metals (copper, aluminum, zinc, lead, nickel, and tin) and the monthly average and domestic sales prices of zinc ingots. The domestic price of zinc ingots is the standard domestic distribution price excluding VAT provided by Korea Zinc.

The LME inventory, precious metals (gold and silver) prices, and weekly and monthly market status comments on the association site could not be confirmed in the public menu. The statistical information sub-statistics screen of the non-ferrous metal statistics and price information bulletin board could not be opened due to a server error (VBScript 800a0009), so only the price and statistics data posted in the bulletin board was used.

Recycled raw materials are monthly published values ​​from the Korea Environment Corporation’s “Recyclable Resources Price Survey” (National Approved Statistics No. 392001). It is surveyed on the 10th of each month and announced on the 26th, and the unit is KRW/kg (including value-added tax, excluding logistics costs) and is the national average. Waste paper and steel scrap are the purchase price of unprocessed raw materials from intermediate processing companies, and waste plastic, waste glass bottles, and waste metal cans are the sales price after intermediate processing, so the actual transaction price may be different even for the same item. The November 2026 version was posted on the Circulating Resources Information Center on November 25, and ABS flakes were omitted from the table as they were not announced (-).

Chinese spot is the SunSirs daily list (11/26) value. HDPE 10,037.50 yuan, PVC 5,080.00 yuan, PP 9,400.00 yuan, LDPE 10,500.00 yuan, etc., and the fluctuation rate is the value compared to 11/25 revealed by SunSirs in the same table.
